plants.name: Helleborus niger
plants.description: An evergreen perennial with leathery, dark green, palmate leaves and nodding, cup-shaped flowers that open pure white and often age to a soft pink. Its blooms appear in the depths of winter, bringing welcome color to dormant gardens.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late autumn to late winter (November to March in the Northern Hemisphere)
plants.location: Native to the mountainous woodlands of central and southern Europe; widely cultivated in temperate gardens in Europe and North America
plants.funFact: Despite its name, the Christmas Rose is not a true rose but a member of the buttercup family, and all parts of the plant are toxic. It can bloom through snow.

plants.name: Camellia japonica
plants.description: A broadleaf evergreen shrub or small tree with glossy dark green leaves and large, showy, rose-like flowers. Hundreds of cultivars exist with single, semi-double, or fully double blooms.
plants.bloomingSeason: Winter to early spring (December to April in the Northern Hemisphere)
plants.location: Native to Japan, Korea, and eastern China; cultivated in the southeastern United States, Western Europe, and mild climates worldwide
plants.funFact: Camellia japonica is the state flower of Alabama, and in Japan it is called 'tsubaki' and has long been associated with the tea ceremony and samurai culture.

plants.name: Protea cynaroides
plants.description: A striking evergreen shrub with the largest flower head of any protea, up to 30 cm across, made of a central cone of tiny flowers surrounded by showy, petal-like bracts. It thrives in the fynbos of the Cape region.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late spring to summer in the Southern Hemisphere, with peak blooming from December to February in some regions and cultivars
plants.location: Native to the fynbos of the southwestern and southern Cape of South Africa; cultivated in Australia, Hawaii, and California
plants.funFact: The King Protea is the national flower of South Africa, and its genus is named after the Greek god Proteus because of the remarkable variety of its forms.

plants.name: Delonix regia
plants.description: A broad, umbrella-shaped tropical tree with feathery, fern-like leaves and spectacular clusters of large flowers that nearly cover the canopy. Each flower has four spreading scarlet petals and one larger petal streaked with white and yellow.
plants.bloomingSeason: Summer in the Southern Hemisphere (December to February), with seasonal blooming in tropical and subtropical regions
plants.location: Native to Madagascar; widely planted in Australia, southern Africa, South America, and the tropics worldwide
plants.funFact: In its native Madagascar the Royal Poinciana is critically endangered in the wild, even though it is one of the most widely planted ornamental trees on Earth.
